explanation: Pointing directly at a person with a single extended index finger can come across as aggressive or accusatory in China; the more polite convention is to gesture with an open hand, palm up, toward the person or object. It's a matter of perceived rudeness rather than a severe taboo, and younger, more casual settings are more forgiving of it.
local_tip: When indicating a person or direction, use an open hand gesture instead of a single pointed finger.

also_check.note: Pointing with a finger is seen as impolite; gesturing with an open hand is preferred.
Index-finger pointing is considered impolite; using the thumb to indicate direction is the common alternative.
Pointing with the index finger is common and generally unremarkable in casual settings.
